title: Study notes
html:
Infection

  • Acute osteomyelitis: S. aureus, haematogenous, metaphysis of children. X-ray normal for 10–14 days (soft-tissue swelling first) → then osteolysis and periosteal reaction. MRI is the earliest test (marrow oedema T1 dark/STIR bright, abscess); US shows subperiosteal fluid in children.
  • Chronic osteomyelitis: sequestrum (dense dead fragment in a lucent bed – CT best), involucrum, cloaca, cortical thickening and diffuse sclerosis. Garré = sclerosing form without sequestrum.
  • Spondylodiscitis: disc narrowing + destruction of BOTH endplates (metastases spare the disc). TB (Pott): slow, gibbus, block vertebra, paravertebral cold abscess.
  • Septic arthritis: effusion, then rapid destruction on both sides of the joint – aspirate.

Osteonecrosis

Aseptic (avascular) necrosis of the femoral head: steroids, alcohol, sickle cell disease, dysbarism. MRI first (double-line sign), then sclerosis, subchondral crescent, flattening and collapse; the joint space stays preserved until late. Septic osteonecrosis = infection with sequestrum.

Joints

  • RA stages: I soft-tissue swelling + juxta-articular osteoporosis → II narrowing + small erosions → III large erosions, subluxations, deformities → IV fibrous/bony ankylosis.
  • AS: starts at the sacroiliac joints (bilateral, symmetric: erosions → pseudo-widening → sclerosis → ankylosis), then Romanus lesions, shiny corners, squared vertebrae, syndesmophytes, bamboo spine, trolley-track and dagger signs.
  • Gout: 1st MTP, punched-out erosions with overhanging edges, tophi, bone density preserved.

Bone tumours – a three-question method

  1. Aggressive or not? (margin, zone of transition, periosteal reaction, cortex, soft-tissue mass)
  2. Where? (epiphysis / metaphysis / diaphysis; central / eccentric / cortical)
  3. Who and what matrix? (age; osteoid = cloudy, chondroid = rings and arcs)
LesionAge / siteKey image
OsteomaSkull, frontal/ethmoid sinusDense ivory round opacity
Osteoid osteomaAdolescent, tibia/femur cortexSmall lucent nidus in dense sclerosis; night pain, aspirin – CT
HaemangiomaVertebral bodyVertical striations, T1 and T2 bright
Simple bone cystChild, proximal humerus/femur metaphysisCentral lucency, fallen fragment
Aneurysmal bone cystChild, metaphysis, eccentricExpansile, septated, fluid–fluid levels
Giant cell tumour20–40 y, epiphysis to subchondral boneEccentric lytic, no sclerotic rim; malignant potential
OsteochondromaMetaphysis, points away from jointCortex and marrow continuous with host bone
EnchondromaHand phalangesLobulated lucency, chondroid calcifications
Osteosarcoma10–25 y, metaphysis around the kneeMixed lysis/sclerosis, sunburst, Codman triangle
Ewing sarcoma5–20 y, diaphysis, flat bonesPermeative, onion skin, big soft-tissue mass
Chondrosarcoma> 40 y, pelvis, proximal femurPopcorn calcifications, endosteal scalloping
Myeloma / plasmacytoma> 50 y, skull, spine, pelvisMultiple punched-out lyses, bone scan often negative
Metastases> 40 y, axial skeletonLytic (lung, kidney, thyroid) or blastic (prostate, breast); ivory vertebra

Exam reflexes

  • Codman triangle = aggressive (malignant primary tumour) – but also seen in infection.
  • Bone scan detects metastases early (metabolic) – except myeloma.
  • Ankylosis appears in AS, RA (late), septic arthritis (sequela) – not in osteoarthritis.
